why: Walk 12: there is almost no ground on the spit under 2 degrees. The crews' yard west of the house (nets, wood, urns, the shrine totem by the path) is levelled and cut and filled under 0.3 m.
Walk 12: the crews' house stands on one levelled pad on the spit's crown, where the slope is 8 degrees. A mound provides the level ground instead of a long apron.
Walk 12: the family house is placed south of the crews' house on its own levelled pad.
Walk 12: the family's yard east of the crews' house (wood, baskets) is levelled and sits between the wall and the water, where the spit slopes 3 to 4 degrees.
When the cove silts, the drop-off where the sounded way ran east of the raft fills to a mud flat just proud of the water.
The peat and mud thrown up out of this season's pit, banked on its south lip.
Spoil thrown out of the water's-edge pit onto its landward lip.
Last season's spoil, banked on the worked-out pit's west lip against the slope.
Trodden flat floor under the open Tag House, where bundles, urns and the handover table stand.
The keeper's levelled yard under and around the stilt hut, where the table, chairs and totem stand.

The spoil berm: the earth dug out to reach the vault, heaped level so a 4 m hollow stands above the marsh pool. Its 4 m blend keeps the ruin court east wall (x 1708) on the lake flat; the climb stair takes the walker up its west bank.

The dug hollow: floor 1.80 m, over the marsh pool at 1.24 m 50 m north by more than 0.5 m. It runs under the whole vault face (x 1736-1741.5) so the face stands on its floor with the berm behind it; three sloped sides at about 27 degrees.
Holds the berm level right behind the vault face. Mounds apply larger first, so this strip is smaller than m-hollow and wins behind it; its 2 m blend meets the back of the face at x 1741.6.
A plane under the two stair flights from the hollow floor (1.80) to the berm rim (5.80); the landing between them is its ground at 3.76 m.

A level bed for the curtain wall: the lake flat tilts 2.7 to 3.2 degrees under the run, over the 2 degree pad fit. Its south arm under k-0 is narrow so its blend stops short of the court colonnade (c-15, x 1689.4).
A plane under the two flights that climb the berm flank from the court (1.60) to the rim (5.80).

The fallen south curtain: the works wall on the road side came down and its rubble grassed over into a bank about 2.5 m high between the coast road (z 6673) and the court arcade (z 6680). From the road it hides the court floor and the berm stair, so the court is first seen through the gate (hidden); the arcade tops still show over it (afar). It meets the spoil berm at its east end.

The fallen curtain bank turns north along the old wall line between the keep stub (k-0) and the court west colonnade (c-15), so from the junction the colonnade shows only above the bank. The blend ends before c-15 (x 1689.4) and k-0 (z 6687.1).
The salvager household's work yard, trodden level with the house platform on its south side.
The third household's sitting yard, trodden level beside the track on the house's north side.
The bank is dug down to a bed where the pier foot comes ashore, so its planks lie on the ground instead of under it.
The bank climbs from the shore path to a rounded hill behind the west door, so the door is set into the hillside with earth over its lintel.
The bank climbs from the street to the hill behind the east door; it stops short of the street on its north side.
The west forecourt is dug down to the door sill; its sides slope back into the hill.
The east forecourt is dug down to the door sill; its sides slope back into the hill.
The way down: a sloped cut from the shore path into the west forecourt.
The way down: a sloped cut from the street into the east forecourt.
The hill closes right up to the back of the west portico, so its lintel is buried in the bank.
The hill closes right up to the back of the east portico, so its lintel is buried in the bank.
The hill is banked hard against the back of the west portico, so the doorway opens straight into the slope with no gap behind.
The hill is banked hard against the back of the east portico, so the doorway opens straight into the slope with no gap behind.
The west portico floor in front of the door stays level with the sill; the portico itself hides the edges.
The east portico floor in front of the door stays level with the sill; the portico itself hides the edges.
Trodden mud banked on the dry strand under the foot of the barge pier's steps, so the bottom tread meets the ground.
Trodden flat corner under the east sleeping shed's store baskets. The shed stands on stilts and has no pad, so the yard is levelled here.
A worn level patch where the west shed keeps its stores, the shed itself up on stilts.
Flat drying ground where the west shed's nets and sack lie.
Levelled reed-store corner by the hatching shed door.
Clutch ground by the totem, a trodden flat with eggs and twig bundles.
Dug dooryard before the overseer's hut, so the threshold meets the ground. The hut's posts stand clear of it.
Earth banked up to the hatching shed door sill. One flight of steps would stand taller than the sill, so the shed has none.
The head of the way down: a level shelf on the lip where the camp path ends and the cut begins.
The upper leg of the way down: a path cut into earth banked against the cliff, falling west at 27 degrees from the head to the turn.
The turn of the way down: a bench of banked earth in the corner of the west bluff, where the upper cut turns back east onto the lower cut.
The lower leg of the way down: a second path cut along the foot of the cliff, falling east at 29 degrees from the turn to the dry shelf at the head of the plank landing.
Trodden flat on the lip above the landing, where the gang mends and grinds its shovels and picks before taking them down to the channel.
The dry sea-level hollow beside the ring-link is filled to the bank either side, so the lane runs on into the tree ring over one stretch of ground.

The hill behind the cave mouth. Skyrim's cave-mouth rock is a shell made for a hillside. This site is flat jungle floor, so the open back of the rock (azimuths 192..305, band 38.30..50.50 m) stood free. The hill's flat top stands 0.24 m over the open band along the back face of the mouth and 13 m west of it, then falls to the floor over 10 m and stops short of the tunnel. Vanilla buries the backs of its cave mouths under hillside. King of the Murkmire sets its mouths at the foot of a rise ringed with cliff pieces.

The foot of the hill. It wraps both flanks of the cave mouth, so the rock rises out of a slope on three sides. The hill falls to the floor in two easy stages, not one steep drop. It stays at least 13 m from the tunnel and the threshold, so the way in is still level.
The crown of the hill: a rounded ridge along its long axis, so the hill rises to a crest with no flat top. The mound's 13 m blend gives the crest its round shape.

The north flank of the hill beside the cave rock, as one slope. It holds 47 m up to the rock's north foot, then blends over 10 m into the ground, which lies at 40 to 41 m around x 3684 to 3686. Flat steps with short blends appear as bare terraces between the hill and the rock.

A mound against the back of the cave rock. The rock's north back corner stood 2 to 12 m clear of the ground between x 3670 and 3674, which left a dark slot behind it. The mound raises the ground to meet the rock 1.5 to 2.5 m under its top edge. Inside the shell, west of the door, the ground falls away.
The top step of a fill against the rock's north back corner, at 50.6 m, level with the back mound at 50.5 m. The rock's back edge stands 0.8 to 1.9 m above it.
The middle step of the same fill. It buries the rock's top, which dips at this corner.
The lowest step of the same fill. It joins the slope down the north flank, so the corner has no hollow between the hill and the rock.
The hill's south shoulder, one even slope from the top of the cave rock's back at 50.5 m down to the jungle floor east of the mouth, falling 0.7 m per metre.
The foot of the south shoulder beside the cave mouth's south jamb. It rises 0.4 m per metre southward from the floor of the opening, so the shoulder meets the floor on an easy slope.
The hill's north shoulder, one even slope from 48.8 m beside the cave rock down to the jungle floor east of it, falling 0.7 m per metre.
Fills the corner between the north shoulder and the cave rock's north side, so the ground meets the rock with no hollow between them.
The north side of the mound behind the cave rock, one slope falling 0.6 m per metre from the mound top to the hill foot at 44.5 m, so the mound has no steep north face.

Walk 12: the cave rock's open back rim at its top rear (x 3665 to 3668, z 4563 to 4570) stood 0.6 to 1.5 m over the hill, the gap the owner saw. This mound lifts the hill to the rim's top (51.2 to 52.0 m) along that stretch, so the rock sinks into the hill.

Walk 12: the seat of the canopy giant on the hill top (t-crown-giant). The tree's root plate needs level ground; a 16 m pad at the height of the crest gives it that, wide enough for the full-size tree's root plate. The 10 m blend keeps the crest round.
A low apron under the south foot of the hill, from x 3646 to 3680. It holds the ground at 41 m for 6 m before it falls to the jungle floor, so the hill's south side comes down in two stages.
The north-west back corner of the cave rock: one rim vertex at x 3666.7 z 4552.7 stood 0.55 m over the hill. The ground there is lifted to the rim so no gap shows behind the rock.
